themeCards.title: Payrolls beat the estimate, and hike odds moved back toward 60%
themeCards.fact: CNBC: August nonfarm payrolls rose 162,000 versus the Dow Jones estimate of 53,000, and the unemployment rate held at 4.1%. AP: the S&P 500 fell 0.4% to 7,718.60. US Treasury: the official 4 September curve printed 4.37% on the 2-year and 4.78% on the 10-year. 财经早茶: swap markets put the September hike back near 60%, and Trump threatened to cut trade with deficit countries if the Fed does not cut.
themeCards.mechanism: A 162,000 print versus 53,000 is why the 2-year went to 4.37% and the S&P 500 closed at 7,718.60, even with unemployment still at 4.1%. CICC (6 September): the jobs beat lowered the employment constraint on a hike, and September still needs the inflation prints to settle the decision. CPI on 11 September, then the FOMC at 02:00 Beijing on 17 September, are the settle.

themeCards.title: Saturday tanker strikes left Hormuz reopening more remote
themeCards.fact: CNBC: WTI settled at $91.48, up 18 cents, and Brent at $96.28, up 76 cents; four commodity vessels transited Hormuz on Thursday versus a 10-day average of about 15. CNN: CENTCOM struck three IRGC tankers on Saturday after IRGC missiles at two US Navy ships. 财经早茶: Tehran said it hit three tankers on unauthorized Hormuz routes, and hopes of reopening look more remote.
themeCards.mechanism: Saturday’s tanker strike keeps a war premium in WTI at $91.48 after a week that already settled Brent at $96.28. Goldman Sachs (5 September): Hormuz flow has recovered about two-thirds, with about five million barrels a day moving as dark ships the AIS count misses, which is why a modest Friday settle can sit beside another shooting day. The next dated Hormuz-flow print, and CPI on 11 September through the energy line, settle whether that premium sticks.

themeCards.title: Gold and bitcoin both sold the Friday hike-duration move
themeCards.fact: Kitco: late-afternoon spot gold was near $4,429.40, down 0.96%, after a low near $4,365. Cointelegraph: bitcoin sold from $81,300 to $78,600 after the jobs print, then $79,500. Cointelegraph: Friday US spot bitcoin ETF inflows were $174.6 million.
themeCards.mechanism: Gold and bitcoin sold the same hike-duration beta, so late-afternoon gold near $4,429.40 and a dip through $78,600 are one book, and Friday ETF inflows of $174.6 million show allocators still added. Glassnode (2 September): spot is boxed between short-term-holder supply below and long-term-holder supply above. CPI on 11 September, through the dollar, is the next print.

themeCards.title: Beijing recapped lenders while the PBOC stopped adding and issuance stayed slow
themeCards.fact: 第一财经: eight central financial firms plan to raise 3600亿元 (CNY360bn), and the Ministry of Finance will issue 3000亿元 (CNY300bn) of special treasury bonds. 第一财经: the PBOC will do 5000亿元 (CNY500bn) of 3-month buyout reverse repo on 7 September, an equal rollover versus 5000亿元 maturing, ending two months of 2000亿元 (CNY200bn) add, after the week of 31 August–4 September drained 14115亿元. 新华财经: Shanghai closed at 3930.12, down 0.30%. 财经早茶 今日图表: Jan–Aug government-bond issuance progress is the slowest for the same period in four years.
themeCards.mechanism: A CNY360bn recap tops up core tier-one capital, and an equal CNY500bn three-month rollover after a 14115亿元 weekly drain leaves the 7-day rate uncut, which is why Shanghai closed at 3930.12. CICC (2 September): swap-implied cut expectations sit at a historically strong level while the 7-day rate has gone uncut this year. The next PBOC take-up and US CPI on 11 September, through risk appetite, are the dated prints.

themeCards.title: Tokyo’s reserve tape confirmed the August yen-buying operation
themeCards.fact: Japan Times: Tokyo’s holdings of foreign securities fell by $87.8 billion at end-August, and authorities spent ¥15.4 trillion ($98.6 billion) through Aug. 26. 华尔街见闻: USD/JPY rose from 155.50 to 156.22 on Friday.
themeCards.mechanism: The $87.8 billion drop in foreign securities is the August yen-buying operation of ¥15.4 trillion hitting the reserve tape, which is why USD/JPY can sit at 156.22 after Friday’s bounce from 155.50. The BOJ decision on 17–18 September is the settle.
